reranked_evidence.snippet: # India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown. Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban. Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained. Police and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government have not commented on the use of sticks and tear gas against protesters. reranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize Cockroach Janata Party activist on hunger strike - Los Angeles Times
reranked_evidence.snippet: * Police in New Delhi forcibly moved education reform activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s Cockroach Janata Party movement for education reform. Delhi police said that Wangchuk was taken to the hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. The Cockroach Janata Party — a play on the name of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party — said in a social media post that the government “forcefully abducted” Wangchuk “without his or his family’s consent” two days before their planned march to India’s Parliament.

reranked_evidence.snippet: # India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown. NEW DELHI (AP) — Supporters of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement demanding educational reforms and government accountability refused to leave their New Delhi protest site Tuesday, a day after their thousands-strong march toward Parliament drew police tear gas, beatings and a new wave of sympathy from across the country. The movement, now attracting professionals and families beyond students, represents a rare public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s government, reviving criticism over its handling of dissent and use of force to respond to protests. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and dozens of his Congress party lawmakers showed their support Tuesday with a sit-in outside Modi’s residence before police forcibly removed them in a dramatic escalation. reranked_evidence.snippet: # Robbie Williams responds to cocaine accusations after viral World Cup Final video. Robbie Williams clarified that the white substance that fell from his face at the 2026 World Cup Final was a mint, and not cocaine. The British singer, 52, addressed a viral video of a live interview he did at the World Cup Final between Spain and Argentina Sunday, in which a white substance appeared to fall from his face and onto his mic. Williams didn’t miss a beat, picking up the white object off the mic and continuing the interview. The “Angels” singer took to Instagram Monday and shared a cheeky video explaining that the white object was a mint. The pop star went viral Sunday for the incident, with some on X accusing him of using cocaine. Although he took the mint off his mic, it ended up going on his forehead after he scratched his head with the same hand.

reranked_evidence.title: Samsung Reduces US Workforce While Expanding Operations in Texas - RS Web Solutions
reranked_evidence.snippet: # Why Samsung is Reducing US Workforce While Expanding in Texas. *Last updated on  by **Souvik Banerjee** on Categories **Technology***. In a significant operational realignment, Samsung Electronics is poised to eliminate hundreds of positions in the United States, concurrently shifting its consumer electronics headquarters from New Jersey to Texas. This strategic move reflects the company’s recalibration amid surging investments in artificial intelligence and intensifying challenges within its mobile and consumer electronics sectors. The South Korean tech behemoth has announced that 739 roles at Samsung Electronics America (SEA) in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, will be affected due to the relocation. The firm has indicated that many of those impacted will receive relocation offers to Texas, while others face termination, as reported by News. “The transition of SEA’s headquarters may precipitate alterations in our workforce configuration, particularly for personnel unable to relocate or for specific functions refined to align with key business objectives,” the company articulated.
